title: Why is Gemini 4 Carbon taking so long?
lede: A team tracing Gemini 4 Carbon on a private bug-fixing eval found it took close to an hour on tasks Opus and Astra finished in minutes, and broke down where the time went.

points: Slower inference explains 16 to 30% of the extra time against Astra and about half against Opus; the rest comes from longer runs.
Carbon took about seven times Astra's steps and eleven times its actions, and processed over sixteen times the input.
Roughly half its steps went on work the ticket never asked for: auditing unrelated code paths and guarding cases already ruled out.
Injecting a check-in every five turns cut one trial from 37 to 28 minutes, suggesting the cause is habit, not missing knowledge.
One tool call per step and re-reading 39% of lines, against 7% for Astra, account for about a quarter of the excess.

points.text: A commenter with separate data confirmed the slowness: about three times the completion time, more than double the output tokens and nearly twice the tool calls.
Commenters split on whether something is broken, such as time to first token, or whether benchmarks like CursorBench show the model is simply thorough.
One reader treats the extra auditing as a feature, since it surfaces distant bugs and subtle dead code a narrower model would miss.
Several want strict instruction following above all; one found their harness was telling the model to go beyond each request.
